Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be dated December 2024 (from 12/18 to 12/23) except for the first one which is August 1, 2024. Let me focus on the December examples first as they seem to follow a similar pattern.

## Analysis of December Examples (2024-12-18 to 2024-12-23)

Looking at Example 1 (Dec 23):
- Model forecasts are consistently LOWER than true outcomes
- The gap widens over the 30-day horizon
- At day 1: Model 69.28 vs True 69.68 (underestimated by 0.40)
- At day 15: Model 69.33 vs True 78.33 (underestimated by 9.00!) - this is massive
- At day 30: Model 69.17 vs True 81.12 (underestimated by 11.95)

Looking at Example 2 (Dec 20):
- Model forecasts are also consistently LOWER
- Day 15: Model 69.10 vs True 77.98 (underestimated by 8.88)
- Day 30: Model 69.73 vs True 80.88 (underestimated by 11.15)

Looking at Example 3 (Dec 19):
- Model forecasts are again LOWER
- Day 15: Model 67.58 vs True 77.98 (underestimated by 10.40)
- Day 30: Model 74.48 vs True 80.96 (underestimated by 6.48)

Looking at Example 4 (Dec 18):
- Model forecasts are again LOWER
- Day 15: Model 69.08 vs True 76.92 (underestimated by 7.84)
- Day 30: Model 67.74 vs True 83.93 (underestimated by 16.19)
 
I notice a consistent pattern of model underestimation across multiple dates. The forecasts consistently trail behind true outcomes, with the divergence growing more pronounced over time. This suggests a systematic bias in the prediction model, particularly at longer horizons.

The sentiment analysis reveals an interesting dynamic. When market sentiment shifts from negative to positive, the model struggles to fully capture the true price trajectory. Specifically, the model seems to have difficulty accurately translating positive sentiment into corresponding price increases.
